results.identification: A bullet‑point synopsis of the UK Conservative Party’s 2015 General Election manifesto (Strong Leadership, A Clear Economic Plan, A Brighter, More Secure Future). It’s an unofficial summary derived from the Conservative Party’s 2015 manifesto.
results.evidence: The header explicitly says “Conservative Party Manifesto 2015 – Summary.” Distinctive 2015 Conservative pledges appear throughout: “Hold an in/out EU referendum by end‑2017,” “Replace the Human Rights Act with a British Bill of Rights,” “extend Right to Buy to Housing Association tenants,” “deliver 3 million new apprenticeships,” “at least £8bn extra [for the NHS] by 2020 to deliver a 7‑day NHS,” “Northern Powerhouse,” “end new subsidies for onshore wind,” “triple lock,” and “raise [the] Inheritance Tax threshold on the family home to £1m for couples.”

results.identification: A user-written, ≤500-word bullet-point summary of the UK Labour Party’s 2015 General Election manifesto, originating as an answer on Politics Stack Exchange in the 2015 ‘manifestos in 500 words’ Q&A thread.
results.evidence: The heading reads “Labour Party Manifesto 2015 – Summary (≤500 words)”. The bullet-point style and the 500-word cap match a well-known Politics Stack Exchange thread from the 2015 UK election where users posted ≤500-word manifesto summaries. The content lists distinctive 2015 Labour pledges (e.g., Budget Responsibility Lock; restore 50p rate and 10p starting rate; abolish non-dom status; freeze energy bills until 2017; reduce tuition fees to £6,000; repeal the Health and Social Care Act; replace the House of Lords with an elected Senate of the Nations and Regions), aligning closely with Labour’s 2015 manifesto.

results.identification: A community-written 500‑word summary of the UK Independence Party (UKIP) 2015 UK General Election manifesto, posted as part of Politics Stack Exchange’s manifesto summary series.
results.evidence: The title line says "UKIP Manifesto 2015 – Summary (≤500 words)" and the bullets align with well-known UKIP 2015 positions: leave the EU via Article 50 and seek a UK–EU FTA; Australian‑style points immigration system and a moratorium on unskilled immigration; scrap HS2; repeal the Climate Change Act and end wind/solar subsidies; oppose an EU army; retain Trident; restrict benefits/health access for recent migrants; end the ECHR/HRA in favor of a UK Bill of Rights. The structured, cross‑policy, bullet‑point format is characteristic of the 500‑word party‑manifesto summaries produced on Politics Stack Exchange for the 2015 UK General Election.

results.identification: An unofficial bullet‑point summary of the UK Liberal Democrats’ 2015 General Election manifesto (“Stronger Economy, Fairer Society: Opportunity for Everyone”), derived from the Liberal Democrats’ 2015 manifesto published by the Liberal Democrats (UK).
results.evidence: The text explicitly uses the 2015 Liberal Democrat slogan “Stronger Economy, Fairer Society: Opportunity for Everyone,” and lists signature 2015 Lib Dem policies: “Five Green Laws,” raising the Personal Allowance to £12,500, a “High Value Property Levy on homes >£2m” (their ‘mansion tax’), pro‑EU with TTIP safeguards and a referendum only on material treaty change, votes at 16 and STV, protecting the Human Rights Act and a Digital Bill of Rights, stepping down the nuclear posture (ending continuous patrols), and mental health parity with extra NHS funding.

results.identification: A community‑written, ≤500‑word bullet‑point summary of the Scottish National Party (SNP) manifesto for the 2015 UK general election, published as part of the manifesto‑summary project on the Politics Stack Exchange (community wiki).
results.evidence: The heading 'SNP Manifesto 2015 – Summary (≤500 words)' indicates a condensed overview rather than the manifesto itself. The bullets match distinctive 2015 SNP positions (e.g., deliver the Smith Commission; oppose Trident renewal; seek a 'double majority' on any EU exit; moratorium on fracking; NHS funding boost routed to Scotland; no focus on independence in this election). The '≤500 words' label and standardized, sectional bullet‑point style are characteristic of the Politics Stack Exchange community‑wiki manifesto‑summary series.

results.identification: A concise summary of the UK Labour Party’s 2015 General Election manifesto (“Britain Can Be Better”), produced as a policy‑commitments overview of Labour’s manifesto under Ed Miliband.
results.evidence: UK‑specific pledges strongly associated with Labour’s 2015 platform: energy bill freeze to 2017; restore the 50p top income tax rate; abolish non‑dom status; mansion tax/tobacco levy to fund NHS staff; repeal NHS competition regime and cap private‑provider profits; abolish employment‑tribunal fees; end the Free Schools programme; public operator option for rail; abolish the Bedroom Tax; OBR audits of manifestos; two‑year wait for in‑work benefits for new EU arrivals; protect the Human Rights Act/ECHR; Constitutional Convention and a Senate of Nations and Regions; National Infrastructure Commission; British Investment Bank.

results.identification: A bullet-point summary of the UK Independence Party (UKIP) 2015 UK general election manifesto, as presented on Wikipedia’s “Policies of the UK Independence Party” page (the ‘Summary of proposals (2015 manifesto)’ section).
results.evidence: Mentions hallmark UKIP 2015 policies: leaving the EU and ending freedom of movement via an Australian-style points system; repealing the Climate Change Act and ending new wind/solar subsidies; cancelling HS2; reopening Manston Airport; allowing ventilated smoking rooms in pubs; decriminalising TV licence non-payment; cutting overseas aid to ~0.2% of GNI and folding DFID into the FCO; free hospital parking; UK fishing policy of a 12‑mile zone and 200‑mile EEZ; protecting under‑10m fleet; and specific UKIP proposals like scrapping DCPC and creating a shale sovereign wealth fund. The heading “Summary of proposals (2015 manifesto)” matches the subsection title used on Wikipedia’s UKIP policies page.

results.identification: A concise policy summary from the UK Liberal Democrats’ 2015 General Election manifesto (Stronger Economy. Fairer Society. Opportunity for Everyone.)—the manifesto’s at‑a‑glance/summary of proposals.
results.evidence: Multiple signature Liberal Democrat 2015 policies appear: “Five green laws”; “reduce nuclear patrol posture” (ending continuous at‑sea deterrence posture); “Proportional voting (STV) … votes at 16 … elected second chamber”; “Digital Bill of Rights … net neutrality … oppose blanket surveillance”; drugs reform with “diversion for possession … medicinal cannabis; move policy lead to Health”; a “£250 annual bonus” for carers; housing measures like “Rent to Own” and “deposit loans for under‑30s”; “banded levy on homes over £2m” (mansion tax); pro‑EU stance; “Green Investment Bank with borrowing powers”; early “net‑zero emissions target by 2050”.

results.identification: A policy-only, de‑rhetoricized summary of the Scottish National Party’s 2015 UK General Election (Westminster) manifesto, ‘Stronger for Scotland,’ derived from the SNP manifesto.
results.evidence: References specific to Scotland and SNP positions, e.g.: "Implement the Smith Commission swiftly and fully"; "Seek further devolution toward full financial responsibility"; "Support continued EU membership with a “double‑majority” requirement for any UK exit"; "Oppose renewal of the UK nuclear deterrent"; "Increase UK health spending (yielding about £2bn extra for Scotland by 2020–21)"; "Maintain free university tuition"; "Retain 1,000 additional police officers"; "Connect Scotland to HS2"; and energy/renewables priorities including "island interconnectors" and "transmission charging reform" that are hallmark SNP/Scotland-focused policies circa 2015.
